newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ's Brash sees Sept pension poll hitting rates.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ's Brash sees Sept pension poll hitting rates.

text.p: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Governor Don Brash said on Wednesday he saw the possibility that September's planned referendum on compulsory superannuation could lead to downward pressure on monetary conditions if the result was a rejection of the plan.
A compulsory superannuation scheme being designed for New Zealand sees all individuals contributing a percentage of their income to a pension scheme approved by the government.
Although the exact terms of the scheme have yet to be released, opinion polls indicate that most voters will vote against the concept in the planned referendum.
"If the referendum looks like passing, then we would expect (markets to exert) downward pressure on conditions," Brash told parliament's Finance and Expenditure Select Committee.
He added that if there was what he called "a surprise result" then the bank might look at issuing a supplementary statement.
It usually only makes routine statements four times a year.
